## Data and two different dimensions

The bundled subset is extracted from ECCC's CANGRD v2023 native grids.
The data originate from homogenized station observations interpolated by ECCC.
Each native cell is nominally 50 km wide. No further spatial interpolation,
resampling, or imputation is performed in this example.

The two observation variables are anomalies of annual mean daily minimum and
maximum temperatures, in degrees Celsius, relative to 1961-1990. Thus $d=2$.
The values are anomalies, not absolute temperatures or annual extreme values.

```{r}
library(GLBFP)
library(ggplot2)
climate <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "cangrd_quebec_1991_2020.csv", package = "GLBFP"))
head(climate[c("i", "j", "year", "tmin_anomaly_c", "tmax_anomaly_c")])
```

For 2020, sites are indexed by $(i,j)$, so $N=2$. For the 1991-2020 sequence,
sites are indexed by $(i,j,\text{year})$, so $N=3$. Adding time changes the index
dimension; it does not add a third observation variable.

```{r}
values <- c("tmin_anomaly_c", "tmax_anomaly_c")
year2020 <- climate[climate$year == 2020L, ]
field2 <- glbfp_field(as.matrix(year2020[values]), as.matrix(year2020[c("i", "j")]),
  units = c("deg C", "deg C"), dependence = "dependent")
field3 <- glbfp_field(as.matrix(climate[values]), as.matrix(climate[c("i", "j", "year")]),
  units = c("deg C", "deg C"), dependence = "dependent")
field2
field3
```

There are 92 sites and 2,760 site-years. The geographic selection is an
incomplete subset of the native integer bounding box; it is not the outline
of Quebec. All selected sites have both measurements for every selected year.
No missing observations are filled. Latitude and longitude are retained as
metadata and are not appended to the density variables.

## Maps retain the native spatial resolution

```{r}
map <- climate[climate$year %in% c(1991, 2005, 2020), ]
map$x_km <- (map$i - min(climate$i)) * 50
map$y_km <- (map$j - min(climate$j)) * 50
ggplot(map, aes(x_km, y_km, fill = tmin_anomaly_c)) +
  geom_tile(width = 50, height = 50) + coord_equal() + facet_wrap(~year) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Tmin anomaly (deg C)") + theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Along native i-axis (km)", y = "Along native j-axis (km)",
       title = "Three time slices of the N=3 field") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Each square represents an observed source-grid value, already interpolated
by ECCC from stations. Smoothing its display would not add observed spatial
detail. These are input maps, not GLBFP density estimates.

## A bivariate density for either index dimension

Use common illustrative bandwidths $b=(0.6,0.6)$, integers $m=(3,3)$, fine
counting-cell widths $b/m=(0.2,0.2)$, and anchor $(-8,-8)$, in temperature units.
Counting cells are half-open, interpolation uses their centres, and unoccupied
cells have zero counts on an unbounded lattice. Display limits do not clamp
or renormalize the density.

```{r}
points <- as.matrix(expand.grid(Tmin = seq(-3, 5, length.out = 201),
                               Tmax = seq(-3, 5, length.out = 201)))
fit2 <- GLBFP_estimate(field2, b = c(.6, .6), m = c(3, 3),
  min_vals = c(-8, -8), max_vals = c(8, 8), grid_points = points)
fit3 <- GLBFP_estimate(field3, b = c(.6, .6), m = c(3, 3),
  min_vals = c(-8, -8), max_vals = c(8, 8), grid_points = points)
plot_density(fit2, "heatmap", labels = c("Tmin anomaly", "Tmax anomaly"),
  title = "Bivariate density of the 2020 sites (N=2)") + coord_equal()
plot_density(fit3, "heatmap", labels = c("Tmin anomaly", "Tmax anomaly"),
  title = "Bivariate density of all selected site-years (N=3)") + coord_equal()
```

The density axes represent the two temperature anomalies. They do not
represent geographic coordinates or time. A high density indicates a
concentration of observed anomaly pairs. Density units are reciprocal squared
degrees Celsius. A 3D surface would add density as its height while keeping
$d=2$. For true $d=3$ observations, use density slices or isosurfaces instead.

Pooling years gives equal weights to the selected site-years. This describes
their finite mixture and does not assert a unique stationary climate law.
There is no correction for geographic cell area; this example computes no
confidence interval under dependence or calibrated climate-trend test. The bandwidth is
illustrative, not claimed to be optimal. Dependence and interpolation
uncertainty are not estimated by this demonstration.

## Exports and provenance

The installed script exports refined density displays with 481 points per
axis, contours, maps and self-contained interactive surfaces:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
source(system.file("examples", "quebec_climate.R", package = "GLBFP"))
```

The denser evaluation grid changes the rendering, not the statistical counting
grid. To estimate uncertainty, a justified dependence method would have to be
specified separately; assigning integer spatial indices is not sufficient.
